name: Mastra & Commander — Operator deck back
symmetry: 180° rotational about 412.5,562.5 on every printing layer — grounds are centre-out radial, ornament and rings are half-paths re-used rotated, the bezel band is radial with a zero-offset shadow. No directional lighting anywhere: a face-down card gives away no orientation.
notes: Backs carry no live text — every glyph is baked.
Layout is 180° rotationally symmetric about the card centre so a card in hand gives away nothing about its orientation.
back-wordmark.svg draws the lockup once inside #wmHalf and re-uses it rotated 180°; edit the group, both copies follow.

back-lattice.svg draws the ornament AND the concentric rings once inside #halfOrn as half-paths (top vertex → bottom vertex), then re-uses them rotated 180°; back-medallion.svg does the same with #mdRings. Never draw a ring as a full closed path with a dasharray — the dash phase would not survive the rotation and becomes an orientation tell.
Ice-chrome ground with the cyan set mark scaled ×13 as the medallion — identical geometry to collector.svg's set mark.
Used for every deck except Entropy: ice, eval, feature, loadout, model, framework, token.

No printing layer may carry a diagonal gradient or an offset drop shadow — both survive a 180° rotation as their own reverse and become an orientation tell. Grounds and the bezel band use centre-out radial gradients; the frame shadow is dy=0.
